why: Per my prereg tree, EXTERNAL_CONFIRMED requires three jointly-satisfied conditions, and all three are met by my own execution results: (1) judge() passed the pure-function admission check - AST inspection found no imports, no IO, no random, no time, no network, and no hardcoded ids, so the assertion layer is admitted as a genuine criterion; (2) per-case agreement with my own ground truth over all pairs is 16/16 = 1.000, which is well above the 0.85 threshold (>=14 of 16); (3) all three phenomena families were correctly classified on at least one instance - negation flip, tail deletion, and connector change each show non-zero detection, so no family is at zero. Because the direction of my finding matches the commissioning repo's published claim that a transferable criterion can see the assertion layer, and because the systematic-failure pattern required for EXTERNAL_DIVERGENT (majority of gt-false pairs returned true) did not occur, EXTERNAL_DIVERGENT is ruled out. EXTERNAL_PARTIAL is ruled out since I cleanly exceed the CONFIRMED threshold and have no family at zero detection. Thus my criterion is internally consistent and transferable on this fresh paper, including the assertion layer. This is a transferability result, not a strong-L3 or absolute claim.
